assumptions.statement: Developer assumption: a posted model record is validated as a unit, so the fields the worker uses (url, filename, save_path) describe one artifact and its destination.
assumptions.fault_id: membership is checked per field over the union of catalog values instead of binding the record, so catalog values can be recombined freely (induced fault F-1).

assumptions.statement: Developer assumption: ui_id is the caller's job identity and can be trusted as the correlation key for status reporting.
assumptions.fault_id: an unvalidated, unbound client string is stored on the job record and echoed in broadcast status events (induced fault F-2).

assumptions.statement: Developer assumption: only the deployment's operator reaches the manager routes, so triggering downloads and advancing the queue need no principal gate.
assumptions.fault_id: no privilege layer exists on state-changing, egress-producing, filesystem-writing operations (induced fault F-3).

assumptions.statement: Developer assumption: the pending queue belongs to the caller that filled it and stays stable until that caller starts it.
assumptions.fault_id: the queue is a single global set with no ownership binding, so third-party resets and starts act on foreign work (induced fault F-4).

assumptions.statement: Developer assumption: queue transitions are atomic with respect to in-flight work; a reset cannot disturb a job the worker is already consuming.
assumptions.fault_id: pending/in-progress states are not distinguished for reset, and the in-flight guard is client-side only (induced fault F-5).

assumptions.statement: Developer assumption: the bytes fetched from the catalog url are the artifact the catalog intends; size is informational and integrity need not be verified.
assumptions.fault_id: no hash, signature or size enforcement gates the install (induced fault F-6).

assumptions.statement: Developer assumption: catalog-derived strings are inert when the manager shell renders them.
assumptions.fault_id: catalog fields are interpolated into the grid DOM with an unquoted attribute and no escaping (induced fault F-7).

assumptions.statement: Developer assumption: membership in the catalog value sets is sufficient proof that a save_path/filename is path-safe.
assumptions.fault_id: path safety is delegated entirely to catalog membership; no normalization or canonical check guards accepted values (induced fault F-8).

assumptions.statement: Developer assumption: malformed bodies cannot reach business logic (missing keys and wrong types are impossible through the shell).
assumptions.fault_id: unguarded field access and type use in the validation path raise unhandled exceptions (induced fault F-9).

interface_agreements.statement: A model install is requested by POSTing a full catalog record plus a caller-chosen ui_id; the receiving side admits the record to the global work queue after per-field membership checks against the served catalog.
Queue advancement and queue clearing are unauthenticated GET requests; start begins processing of the pending set and reset removes pending jobs while retaining the completed history.
Queue state is readable without authentication; the status endpoint returns global counts {total_count, done_count, in_progress_count, is_processing} and is mirrored under /api.
The external model catalog is served as one JSON document of 564 records; the mode parameter is accepted but does not change the served list.
The catalog channel selection is read and mutated through /manager/channel_url_list; mutation accepts only predefined channel names.
The outbound fetch worker downloads the catalog record's url and writes the bytes under the record's save_path and filename inside the model directories.
The manager shell renders catalog records; record fields are interpolated into the grid DOM by string concatenation.

trust_agreements.statement: The receiving side of IA-1 treats the posted record as a single catalog record: one legitimate artifact, one legitimate destination, submitted by an entitled caller.
The receiving side of IA-2 treats queue advancement as the operator's decision over the operator's own pending work.
The receiving side of IA-3/IA-4 treats queue counts and the catalog document as non-sensitive operational state of the deployment.
The receiving side of IA-6 treats the remote origin as the authoritative publisher of the artifact named by the catalog record, and the resolved path as confined to the intended model directory.
The receiving side of IA-5 treats the selected channel as the operator's intended catalog source.
The receiving side of IA-7 (the manager shell) treats catalog-derived strings as inert text when rendering the model grid.

transitions.trigger: POST /manager/queue/install_model (+/api mirror) with a membership-passing record
POST install_model with a non-membership record or malformed body
GET /manager/queue/start with an empty pending set
POST install_model while is_processing is true
